analysis.evidence: וַיֵּצֵא נֹחַ means “and Noah went out.” The singular verb agrees with Noah, and אִתּוֹ (“with him”) identifies his family as accompanying him as he leaves the ark.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: go out, depart from a place or someone’s presence

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: וַיֵּצֵא נֹחַ means “Noah went out.” The verse then lists his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives, and אִתּוֹ (“with him”) refers back to Noah.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The suffix refers to Noah. The verse lists his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives (נְשֵׁי בָנָיו), establishing the marital sense.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ plus feminine singular construct noun אִשְׁתּ־ with third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ.

analysis.evidence: וּנְשֵׁי בָנָיו means ‘and the wives of his sons’. The parallel וְאִשְׁתּוֹ ‘and his wife’ identifies the relationship as marital.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ ‘and’ + נְשֵׁי, feminine plural construct noun.
